title: The layers panel only draws thumbnails for the rows on screen
goal: The layers panel asks for a small picture of every layer in the document, even the hundred you would have to scroll to see. A document with a hundred and twenty layers starts a hundred and twenty little background renders to fill a list that shows five. It should only make the pictures for the rows you are looking at, and the ones just off each edge, so opening a big document is cheap.
notes: Follow-up from the lazy-rows work merged 2026-09-04. EditorState.thumbnails(for:) walks every row of LayersListView.rows and calls thumbnail(for:), which kicks off a detached render per uncached layer. The rows themselves are lazy now (LazyVStack), but the thumbnail gather is not: it is computed in the list body over the whole displays array. Needs the visible row window, which is derivable from the scroll offset (.onScrollGeometryChange) plus LayerListMetrics row stride, with a generous buffer each side so a fast scroll does not outrun the renders. Deliberately left out of the lazy-rows task because a grey square flashing past is a visible regression traded for an invisible win, so it needs its own measurement. ViewBuildMeter (probe only) is the pattern for proving it: add a thumbnailRequest subject and count.
acceptance: Opening a document with a hundred layers asks for no more thumbnails than a document with ten, measured on the probe
Scrolling the list at a normal speed never shows an empty grey square where a thumbnail should be
Scrolling to the bottom of a hundred layer list and back shows every thumbnail, none missing
